transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because something’s been happening that I’m not handling as well as I’d like. I keep hearing Garrett’s voice — very clearly — like he’s right behind me when I’m out on the trail, or sometimes when I’m in my painting room.

I know that probably sounds… concerning. Part of me knows he’s dead, I do know that. But in the moment it feels completely real, like he’s actually there. I wasn’t sure if that’s the kind of thing I should come in for, but… it’s been hard to ignore.
Is it always Garrett's voice that you hear?

Mostly, yes. I mean… I don’t want to overstate it, but when it happens, it’s Garrett’s voice. It’s very clear, like he’s standing right behind me on the trail, or in my painting room. I know he’s dead — I do know that — but in the moment it feels completely real.
Do you see or feel anything unusual when you hear Garrett's voice?

I don’t really see anything, no… at least not like an actual figure or anything. It’s more that I hear him so clearly, like he’s standing right behind me, especially on the trail or in my painting room. And for a second it feels… real. I know that probably sounds strange, and I do know he’s dead, but in the moment it doesn’t feel like just a memory.
How long have you been hearing Garrett's voice?

It’s been… about a month, I guess. Since Garrett died. I mean, not every second or anything, but this whole thing has sort of been unfolding over the past month. Is that… the kind of timeline you mean?
Does hearing Garrett's voice cause you significant distress?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but it is distressing. That’s really why I came in. When I hear Garrett’s voice, it’s so clear—like he’s right behind me on the trail or in my painting room—and even though part of me knows he’s dead, in that moment it feels completely real. It scares me, honestly. Is that… does that make sense?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since Garrett passed away?

I… I don’t know if I’d say “most of the time.” I mean, of course I’ve been sad—Garrett died, so it would be strange if I wasn’t. But I’m not sure I’m tracking it clearly enough to say it that way. I don’t want to overstate it. How do you usually mean “most of the time”?
Have you lost interest in activities you normally enjoy since Garrett passed away?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I still try to do things, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve completely stopped functioning. But the things that usually keep me steady—painting, playing guitar, rehearsing at the theater, even sitting with patients—just feel… flat. Like I’m going through the motions, and I can’t really reach the part of me that used to care about them.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of “lost interest” you mean, but… yes, something like that.
Do you feel hopeless about the future?

I’m… not sure. I don’t want to say “hopeless” if that sounds too absolute. I can still imagine that things might get better, at least in theory.

But lately the future feels kind of… hard to picture, I guess. Like I’m just trying to get through the day without making too much of a mess of things. Does that count as hopeless, or is that different?
Have you been having thoughts of worthlessness since Garrett passed away?

I… yeah, I think so. I’m not proud of that, and I don’t want it to sound dramatic.

But I keep going back over everything—every last conversation with Garrett, all the things I said or didn’t say. And then with work, the patient sessions I cancelled… I keep thinking I failed them too. Like I’m letting everyone down.

Sometimes it turns into this feeling that people would probably be better off if I just… wasn’t in the way. I know that may not be the right way to put it, but that’s what it feels like.
Do you feel guilty about Garrett's death?

Yes… I do.

I know, logically, I may not have been able to change what happened, and I’m trying not to make it all about me. But I keep replaying every last conversation with Garrett, looking for where I missed something or said the wrong thing, or didn’t do enough.

And then it sort of spreads to everything else—like the patient sessions I cancelled. I start convincing myself I failed him, and then I failed them too. It gets to this place where I feel like everyone would be better off if I just… wasn’t in the way.

I’m sorry, I don’t know if that’s answering it right.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual since Garrett passed away?

A little, yes… though my wife would probably describe it more clearly than I can.

She says sometimes I’m pacing around the house, moving papers from one place to another like I’m being driven by a motor. And then other times I’ll just sit at the kitchen table and it’s like I’m slowed way down… she’ll ask me something simple and it takes me forever to answer.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… yes, I think there’s been some of that.
Have you found it harder to make decisions since Garrett passed away?

I’m not sure… maybe a little, but I don’t know if I’d call it harder in a major way.

I do find myself second-guessing things more, even small choices, but that may just be me being distracted or tired. I don’t want to overstate it. If you mean like being unable to make decisions at all, I don’t think it’s quite that… at least I don’t think so.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your physical activity level or movement since Garrett passed away?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but my wife has noticed it more than I have.

She says I’ll pace around the house and keep rearranging papers, like I can’t settle down. And then other times I’ll just sit at the kitchen table and everything seems slowed down—she’ll ask me something simple and it takes me a long time to answer.

So… yes, I guess there have been changes. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure or interest in since Garrett passed away?

I wish I could say yes. I mean… I still try to do things, because I know I’m supposed to.

Painting, playing guitar, rehearsing at the theater—those used to kind of anchor me. Even sitting with patients, honestly, used to feel meaningful. Lately it all just feels… flat. Like I’m going through the motions of a life that stopped meaning anything.

I don’t know if that answers it the right way, but… no, not much really feels pleasurable right now.
How long have you been having these thoughts of worthlessness?

Um… pretty much since Garrett passed, I think. At first I told myself it was just normal guilt, you know, going over things after someone dies.

But it’s been… persistent. I keep replaying every last conversation I had with him, and then it spreads to other things too—like patient sessions I cancelled. I start convincing myself I failed everyone somehow.

I know that may sound excessive. I’m not trying to be dramatic. It just… keeps coming back, this sense that I’m in the way, and that people might be better off if I weren’t. Is that what you mean by worthlessness?
Have you experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as seeing things that aren't there, since Garrett passed away?

Um… yes. I’ve been a little embarrassed to say it that way, because I know how it sounds.

It’s not so much seeing things, exactly. It’s more that I hear Garrett’s voice. Sometimes it’s as clear as if he’s right behind me—like when I’m out on the trail, or in my painting room. Part of me knows he’s dead, of course, but in the moment it feels… completely real.

I’m not trying to be difficult or dramatic. That’s actually part of why I came in. Does that make sense?
Have you been experiencing these intense yearnings or longing for Garrett for more than a few months?

Not more than a few months, no. It’s been… about a month, since Garrett died.

I know it probably feels very intense for only that amount of time, but that’s the honest timeline. This whole thing has really been unfolding over these past few weeks.
Would you say that the feeling of things being flat and uninteresting is present most of the day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I can still do things, technically. I can sit with a guitar or go into the painting room, and I show up where I’m supposed to show up.

But most of the day it all feels… flat. Like the things that usually anchor me—painting, guitar, rehearsing at the theater, even work with patients—are sort of unreachable. I’m going through the motions, I guess.

I don’t want to overstate it, but it does feel like the meaning has drained out of almost everything. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have your feelings of sadness and loss of interest in activities been present for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say.

I might have tried to make it sound more manageable before, but the depressed, shut-down part has really been there most days for… about four months now. Most of the day, too, not just little moments.

It feels a little hard to admit it that plainly, but yes—that’s the honest answer.
Have your feelings of sadness and loss of interest in activities been present for at least two weeks?

Yes… at least two weeks. I mean, more than that, honestly.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but the depressed, shut-down part has been going on for about four months now. Most days, anyway. Does that fit what you’re asking?
